title: Predictive upgrade pacing with tenant QoS reservations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Upgrading dedicated GPU pools currently relies on fixed drain rates and static eviction budgets which cause either unnecessary throttling of rollouts or intermittent SLO regressions for latency-sensitive tenants. We need a more nuanced controller that can pace upgrades using demand forecasts and explicit short-term QoS reservations so we can complete upgrades faster while ensuring tenants with tight SLAs are not impacted.

This ticket implements a predictive upgrade pacing system composed of: 1) a forecast component that consumes recent per-tenant request/latency patterns to predict capacity need during a drain window; 2) a token-based QoS reservation API where tenants (or system policy) can request short-term capacity guarantees for critical workloads; 3) an upgrade orchestrator that negotiates with the autoscaler to pre-warm capacity and performs phased eviction buckets based on predicted slack; and 4) runtime telemetry gates that can pause or speed up the rollout based on live SLO signals.

Goals:
- Reduce total upgrade time for a full dedicated pool by >25% for typical workloads with mixed-criticality tenants.
- Eliminate P50 and P95 latency regressions for tenants with QoS reservations during upgrades.
- Provide auditably safe rollback/hold points tied to LTS channel gating rules.

Out of scope: model binary compatibility checks (handled by model onboarding), permanent tenant prioritization policies across all clusters (this ticket is for short-lived upgrade reservations only).
acceptance_criteria: Predictive controller exposes /reserve-qos (internal API) allowing reservation creation with duration and qps/slots specified
Upgrade orchestrator integrates forecast output and issues pre-warm autoscaler requests at least 5 minutes before planned evacuations
Rollout is divided into eviction buckets; each bucket has a computed safe capacity delta and yield threshold based on live SLO metrics
Demonstrated staging run: upgrade of a 200-GPU pool completes at least 20% faster than baseline without causing >5% increase in P95 for reserved-tenants
Telemetry dashboard shows per-tenant reservation usages, forecasted slack, and rollout gate status for debugging and postmortem
Operator runbook covers manual pause/resume and emergency rollback tied to LTS channel gate failures
implementation_steps: Design protobufs for QoS reservation API and add migration to control-plane DB
Add forecasting microservice using recent 15m/1h sliding windows; simple ARIMA baseline then swap for light-weight LSTM if needed
Extend upgrade controller: accept forecast, compute eviction buckets, call autoscaler API for pre-warm and soft-drain signals
Implement per-tenant short-lived reservation enforcement in scheduler: mark reserved slots and exempt from eviction decisions until reservation expires
Add telemetry: Grafana panels for reservation consumption, SLO delta during bucket drains, and upgrade gate boolean metrics
Write integration tests with simulated traffic (locust) and a synthetic tenant mix (latency-sensitive, batch, best-effort)
Run staged rollout in canary cluster, then LTS-staged channels with automated gate checks and manual oversight
Create operator runbook and customer-facing notice templates for tenants impacted by LTS gating policies
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting completed; agreed on conservative default reservation size (5% of pool capacity per critical tenant) and fallback policy to best-effort when capacity exhausted
2026-03-04: Prototype forecasting service (ARIMA) implemented in rust-microsvc; returns 5m and 30m horizon forecasts from historical 1h window
2026-03-06: QoS reservation API schema drafted (proto) and added DB migration draft; awaiting schema review from storage team
2026-03-08: Scheduler exemption logic spike showed race condition during concurrent reservations — added optimistic locking plan and sequencer solution
2026-03-10: Integration harness skeleton built; running synthetic mix against a 32-GPU test pool to tune eviction bucket sizing
decisions: Use short-lived reservations (max duration 15 minutes) instead of permanent priority tiers to keep operator complexity low
Forecasting will start with ARIMA baseline for stability; if errors exceed thresholds after 2 weeks we will evaluate an LSTM model
Eviction buckets will be sized using a 95th-percentile forecasted slack minus safety margin (default 10%)
Autoscaler pre-warm request uses a soft allocation API (does not immediately evict) to avoid double-allocations in edge cases
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-reserving capacity reduces upgrade throughput — Mitigation: conservative defaults and per-upgrade global cap (10% of pool)
Risk: Forecast regressions cause SLO breaches — Mitigation: live gate checks halt upgrades if P95 increases by >7% versus baseline
Risk: DB contention from frequent reservations — Mitigation: sequencer and optimistic locking; reserve cache in controller to reduce writes
notes_for_reviewers: Review API proto for backward compatibility with current autoscaler handshake
Check forecast service resource footprint; we aim for <0.5CPU and <256MB RAM per deployment in canary
Validate operator runbook rollback steps align to LTS channel gating policy and legal/enterprise notice requirements
